title: MonoidProduct: a Lean formalization of the quantum query complexity of the semigroup product problem
description:
A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization, over Mathlib, of the results of The quantum query complexity of the semigroup product problem by Troy Lee and Miklos Santha. The problem is to compute a product x1···xn in a fixed finite semigroup, when one query reveals one input element and the multiplication table is given.

The product breadth β is the smallest bound such that every input word has a subsequence of at most β letters with the same product. For nontrivial finite commutative aperiodic monoids the bounded-error quantum query complexity is Θ(min{n, √(nβ)}), and a monoid with aperiodicity index k has β = O(k log(|M|+1) log log(|M|+2)). For monoids with a stable partial order whose minimum is the identity, the complexity is at most √(n+1)((β+2) log(n+2))O(log(β+2)), with applications to the best time to buy and sell stock problem and to products of unitriangular tropical matrices. For arbitrary finite aperiodic semigroups of order N−1, the complexity is at most min{n, √n logO((N log(N+2))1/3)(n+2)}.

The development builds on the QuantumQueryComplexity library and on the Rao–Bell–Chueluecha–Warnke sunflower bound. The Lean sources are sorry-free; a checks file included in the default build verifies with #guard_msgs that the headline theorems depend on exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
